newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds close slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds close slightly higher.

text.p: Singapore government bonds closed higher across the board in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Thursday.

"Bond prices were marked up slightly after a small fall in the interbank rate. There's a good inflow of funds coming into the market from the region. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.

Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.63/98.68 compared with Wednesday's close of S$98.46/98.51, September 2001 at S$97.48/97.53 against S$97.26/97.31 and June 2003 at S$95.48/95.53 from $S95.26/95.31.
The overnight interbank offered rate fell to 3/4 5/8 percent versus Wednesday's 1-1/8 1 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.40/1.35 percent against Wednesday's yield of 1.73/1.68 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.75/1.70 percent from 1.90/1.85 percent.
